solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chief's border guarded by friend

indicators.note: something guarded by another has that other standing round it, so the friend word wraps the border word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A leader's frontier is kept safe by an ally.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Chief' stands for 'is', a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal can mean first in importance, principal, so it is a synonym of chief as an adjective.

clue.text: Rescue about 150 on train

parts.note: re is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about, concerning
CL is 150 in Roman numerals
to train a gun on something is to aim it

explanation.surface: A rescue operation involves around a hundred and fifty people aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces; in a down clue the last piece sits below the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or save it, a synonym of rescue as a verb.

clue.text: Pattern in soft earth

definitions.meaning: a template or form used to shape things, as in casting
loose crumbly soil rich in humus

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a casting form is a pattern, and loose rich topsoil is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Neat lady artists converted to become members of religious sect

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy women painters undergo a religious conversion and join a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' fits the religious surface but is the anagram signal; 'to become' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the common name for Mormons, adherents of the Church of Jesus Christ founded in America.

clue.text: Behind soldier see heartless people in shades

indicators.note: behind places the second piece after the soldier word

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the people word

parts.note: souls are people, as in a village of 200 souls

explanation.surface: Behind a soldier you see cruel people wearing sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link inviting the solver to look; 'shades' suggests sunglasses but here means sunshades.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasols are sunshades, umbrellas carried to give shade from the sun.

clue.text: Green stone fairy placed on spot

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A green gem placed on a mark by a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed on' is a link: in a down clue the fairy sits above the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, the gem variety of olivine.

clue.text: Runs of cards starting with king

indicators.note: starting with puts the king letter at the front of the cards word

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
aces are playing cards

explanation.surface: A run of cards in a game beginning with a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are runs, contests of speed, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: You must tell me what to do if mouth contains poison!

definitions.meaning: an urging to say what one is holding back, an idiom for speak up

definitions.text: what to do if mouth contains poison!
definitions.meaning: literally expel the substance from the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to speak out; taken literally it means eject from the mouth what is in it.

clue.text: Aperture in instrument plugged with open fabric

indicators.note: something plugged with another has that other stuffed inside it

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument
net is an open-meshed fabric

explanation.surface: An opening in a musical instrument stuffed with mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent-shaped opening or window in a vault or dome, so an aperture.

clue.text: Opposing procedure and fighting against board

indicators.note: against means next to, so the fighting word is set beside the board word

parts.note: a counter is a shop's board or table
action is fighting, as in killed in action

explanation.surface: An opposing procedure combined with fighting against a governing board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; 'board' suggests a committee but is a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Counteraction is action taken in opposition, a procedure that works against another.

clue.text: Perch by post where English journey may finish

parts.note: to land is to perch, as a bird alights
to send is to post a letter

explanation.surface: A bird alights beside a fence post at the end of an English trek.
explanation.walkthrough: LAND'S END is the far western tip of Cornwall, where end-to-end journeys across Britain start or finish; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, a classic end point for long walks and rides.

clue.text: See 4
This person's a good editor, as portrayed

parts.note: this person is the setter, so this person is becomes I am, shortened

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of being a fine editor in a self-portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Imaged means pictured or depicted, a synonym of portrayed as a past participle.

clue.text: The Emerald Isle? Somewhere much further north

definitions.text: The Emerald Isle? Somewhere much further north

parts.words: The Emerald Isle? Somewhere much further north
parts.note: the Emerald Isle is Ireland, but read literally an island of green is the big Arctic island far to the north

explanation.definitionFit: The huge Arctic island has a name literally meaning a green land, though it is mostly ice.

clue.text: Words at foot of page giving indication of monetary amount

definitions.meaning: the instruction printed at the bottom of a page, abbreviated PTO, telling the reader to flip it
a firm's total sales revenue over a period

explanation.definitionFit: The bottom-of-page instruction asks the reader to flip the sheet; in business the word is gross sales takings.

clue.text: Rubbish on a piece of furniture that can be shifted round

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Junk dumped on a piece of furniture that can be moved about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotatable can be turned on an axis, moved round in a circle.

clue.text: Chemical compound with lead affected doctor's alter ego

indicators.note: affected means altered or influenced, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil other self of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: A chemical compound containing lead has changed a doctor's other personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges LEAD into ALDE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldehydes are a class of organic compounds containing a CHO group, such as formaldehyde.

clue.text: Name assumed by boss, an enthusiastic swimmer

indicators.note: a thing assumed by another is taken into it, so the name letter goes inside the boss word

parts.note: a leader is a boss

explanation.surface: A boss takes on an alias and turns out to be a keen swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander is the legendary lover who swam across the Hellespont each night, hence a keen swimmer.

clue.text: Queen leads my people, with diamonds bedecked in the Lords?

indicators.note: leads puts the Queen letters at the front, ahead of the rest

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
mine can mean one's own family, as in me and mine
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: The monarch heads her subjects, while peers in the House of Lords wear jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers in the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber, wear robes trimmed with white fur; 'with' is a link and the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial robes of peers are trimmed with stoat fur, so they are fur-trimmed in that way.

clue.text: Bit of grub accounting for one disease found in bird

indicators.note: found in places the disease and one inside the bird word

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
TB is tuberculosis, a disease
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scrap of food explains why a bird has caught an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel of food, so a small piece of grub.

clue.text: Person with confidential info is nerd, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells you a geek has secret information, or so they imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within an organisation with access to privileged information.

clue.text: Lander crashing in grass

indicators.note: crashing means smashing up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A space lander comes down hard in a grassy field.
explanation.definitionFit: Darnel is a weedy ryegrass that grows among cereal crops.

clue.text: Contributor to baffling office jargon

indicators.note: Contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone adds to the confusing language of the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal specialist vocabulary, a synonym of jargon.

clue.text: Mum needs time with hair — it needs to lie flat

parts.note: ma is a word for mum, mother
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Mother needs time to sort her hair so it lies flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed's padded base is laid flat to be slept on, a playful description of the object.

clue.text: Ways Greek island gets reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the island's name is heard rather than written

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: Routes on a Greek island get covered in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are ways, routes for travel, matching the plural noun.

clue.text: I'd grab iron and work — see me in the kitchen!

indicators.note: to work is to knead or shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A homemaker grabs the iron and gets busy; come and find me in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridged drying surface beside a sink is found in a kitchen, the clue playfully speaking as the object.

clue.text: Duck escaping from wide expanse of water on road in city

indicators.note: escaping from means leaving, so the duck letter is taken out of the wide word

parts.note: broad means wide
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
a ford is a shallow crossing where water covers a road

explanation.surface: A duck flees from a broad lake beside a road in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird but is zero; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Guarantee Conservative will escape blame

indicators.note: escaping means getting away, so the Conservative letter leaves the blame word

parts.note: censure is blame or strong criticism

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is sure to avoid criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, a synonym of guarantee as a verb.
